originalTitle: Elon Musk's Tesla posts cash burn as capex surges on AI, robotaxi push
simplifiedContent: Tesla, a car company owned by Elon Musk, spent more money than it made in the last quarter, which is known as a "cash burn". This happened because the company is investing heavily in new technologies like artificial intelligence and self-driving cars, also known as "robotaxis". Even though Tesla sold more cars than expected and its energy storage business did well, the company still lost $1.1 billion. This matters because investors are watching to see if Tesla can grow its business in areas like autonomy and robotics, especially since the regular car market is getting more competitive. Overall, Tesla's spending on new technologies is a key focus for investors right now.

originalTitle: Google quarterly cloud revenue growth beats expectations
simplifiedContent: Google just released its quarterly earnings report, and its cloud revenue grew 82% from last year, which is even better than expected. This growth is largely due to many big companies wanting to use Google's artificial intelligence (AI) services. This is good news for Google's parent company, Alphabet, as it helps balance out the high costs of investing in AI. Google's search business is also doing well, with more advertisers using its AI features. Overall, Google's strong cloud and search businesses are helping to drive its growth.

originalTitle: US stocks today: S&P 500, Nasdaq close lower amid mixed show by tech stocks ahead of earnings
simplifiedContent: Here's what happened in the US stock market today: the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, which are like big groups of stocks, ended the day lower. This happened because some technology stocks, like software companies, did poorly, while others, like chip makers, did well. Investors are being careful because some big companies, like Alphabet and Tesla, are about to release their earnings reports, which can affect the market. Additionally, higher oil prices and global tensions are making investors worry about inflation, which is causing the market to be unpredictable. This mix of good and bad news is making it hard for the market to make up its mind, even though some people are still feeling optimistic about artificial intelligence.

originalTitle: Yen Rebound Ebbs After Brief Rally on Outlook for BOJ Rate Hikes
simplifiedContent: The Japanese yen recently dropped to its lowest value against the US dollar in over 35 years. It briefly rallied, or increased in value, when investors thought that the Bank of Japan might raise interest rates faster than expected. However, this rally didn't last and the yen's value slid again. This matters because changes in the yen's value can affect trade and investments in Japan. The possibility of interest rate hikes by the Bank of Japan is what caused the brief rally, showing that investors are paying close attention to the bank's decisions.

originalTitle: Two-year yields hit 17-month high on oil surge, Fed fears
simplifiedContent: The interest rate on 2-year US government bonds, also known as the 2-year yield, has reached its highest point in 17 months. This happened because of a recent surge in oil prices and concerns about what the Federal Reserve (the US central bank) might do next. When oil prices rise, it can cause inflation, which is a worry for investors. This increase in the 2-year yield is significant because it shows that investors are expecting the Federal Reserve to take action, possibly by raising interest rates. As a result, investors are preparing for potential changes in the economy.

originalTitle: Gold firms to two-week peak on softer dollar, Fed outlook in focus
simplifiedContent: The price of gold has gone up to its highest point in two weeks. This happened because the value of the US dollar has gone down, which can make gold more attractive to buy. The Federal Reserve, which is like a bank for banks, is also being closely watched, as their future actions might affect the price of gold. This matters because when the dollar is weaker, gold prices often go up, and investors are waiting to see what the Federal Reserve will do next. As a result, gold has become a more popular investment, which is why its price has increased.
